sections.heading: Just a lot, honestly
sections.body: Okay so today was, um, kind of a lot actually—I don’t even know where to start. I keep meaning to tell people things like that and then I just don’t, and I’ve been thinking about that all day because I don’t actually know if I want it or if I just wanted her to think I’m the kind of person who says yes—that’s a thing I do. So lunch—I went to that place on Fifth with the bad sign, the one where the T is falling off, had the same thing I always have; I need to stop going there actually, it’s not even good, I just go because it’s close and I don’t have to think about it. And then, okay, the thing I actually keep circling back to: I think I’m just tired. That’s most of it. I’ve been going to bed at like 1 and getting up at 6 and telling myself that’s sustainable and it’s very obviously not. I said I’d fix that in August. It’s September. That was the day. It was fine. It was actually a pretty good day, I think, I just—yeah. It was a good day.

sections.heading: Deploy drama & Thursday plans
sections.body: I guess work. The deploy we’d been putting off since like the middle of August finally went out this morning and, honestly, I was expecting it to be a disaster? But it wasn’t—it went fine. Marcus stayed on the call with me until like 9:15, which he didn’t have to do, and I should tell him that. The deploy went out and then nothing broke for like four hours, which felt suspicious but okay. Then I had that one‑on‑one with Priya, which, yeah. She asked me if I wanted to lead the migration work next quarter and I said yes way too fast—like immediately. Oh, back to work stuff—I realized this afternoon that the migration thing Priya mentioned is actually going to conflict with the thing Marcus is planning for October, and I don’t think either of them knows. I should probably say something, but I’m not going to say anything until Thursday because I don’t want to be the person who brings that up on a Friday. Still, I should say something.

sections.heading: Finally called Mom
sections.body: Oh — I also finally called my mom back. She's been calling for like a week and I keep letting it go to voicemail, not because I don't want to talk to her, it's just, I don't know, it's always a forty minute call and I never have forty minutes. But I called her today walking back from lunch and she sounded good. She's doing the garden thing again. She sent me pictures of the tomatoes. They look, honestly they look kind of sad, but I told her they look great. That's fine. That's a fine lie.

sections.heading: Sam texted me
sections.body: Sam texted me—first time since, what, March? It was completely normal, just "hey saw this and thought of you" with a link, and I stared at it for probably ten minutes trying to figure out how to respond in an equally normal way. I ended up sending back like three words, which is probably fine, but I've been thinking about it on and off all day and I don't love that I've been thinking about it all day. It's been six months; I thought I was further along than this. Apparently not.
